prompt: Propose statistical checks for a larger sample while stating chance-failure behavior and the claim being tested.
kind: STATISTICAL TEST PLAN ONLY — NOT EXECUTED
answer: For a larger predeclared sample, state the null as the requested standard-normal innovation distribution under the chosen draw protocol, not calibrated market returns. Fix sample size, shape, seed/task allocation, diagnostic methods and rejection thresholds before observing draws; do not retry seeds until passing. Check mean, variance with a stated denominator, tail/bin frequencies and distributional shape; add lag/cross-column diagnostics for the dependence claims actually being assessed. For illustration, under independent N(0,1) draws the mean has variance1/n; Chebyshev gives P(|mean|>=sqrt(1/(n*alpha)))<=alpha, a conservative predeclared chance-failure bound, not a calibration test for all distribution features. For variance or goodness-of-fit tests, specify the null distribution, quantile/method, estimated parameters and justified significance level; adjust for multiple tested features/streams or report an exploratory scope. A valid generator can fail a random diagnostic by chance, and a pass cannot prove normality, independence or generator quality. Retain failures and investigate against predeclared rules rather than tightening/relaxing gates after seeing the sample. No larger-sample moment/distribution/dependence test or Monte Carlo acceptance is run in this batch.
